name: Eric Swalwell
role: U.S. Representative from California (2013-2026); 2019 presidential and 2026 California gubernatorial candidate
summary: Swalwell is a mainstream Democrat best known for advocating a federal ban and buyback of assault weapons. He has backed a public option and coverage for all, the Green New Deal, higher taxes on the wealthy, abortion rights and LGBT equality, and in 2026 campaigned on abolishing ICE and taxing corporations. Much of his available record is from his 2019 presidential campaign.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Cosponsored Medicare for All in 2019 and said he wants coverage for all, with a public option and private plans kept; called Medicare for All 'the obvious solution' but opposed eliminating private insurers.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Supported raising the federal minimum wage to $10.10 (2013 era bill); no recent statement on a larger increase.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Said the wealthy should pay more taxes, backed raising the payroll tax cap, and in 2026 proposed a new corporate tax.

unions-good.rationale: Cosponsored the PRO Act; presented himself as labor-friendly in 2026.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He proposes a mandatory independent AI audit with liability, conditions state support on labor standards and backs corporate tax changes; these are several specific measures, not a general tightening, so +1.

cut-welfare.rationale: He pledges to protect and expand Medi-Cal and income supports, but also criticises homelessness spending that does not measure results; he does not address the dependency claim, so -1.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Backed ending bulk data collection under the PATRIOT Act and restricting domestic phone monitoring (2014), but voted for cybersecurity data sharing.

limit-guns.rationale: Proposed a national ban and mandatory buyback of assault weapons, universal background checks and a ban for domestic abusers, but said he has no problem with people owning handguns or rifles and rejected broad confiscation.

empower-police-military.rationale: Mixed record: favored more resources for state and local law enforcement (2019) but also said he would slash the defense budget.

decide-locally.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

rehabilitation.rationale: He favors treatment, diversion and meaningful reintegration over unnecessary incarceration.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Stated support for full LGBT equality including the freedom to marry.

abortion-legal.rationale: Said abortion should be accessible without restrictions and voted against the 2013 20-week ban.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: He proposes reparative wealth-building programs for descendants of slavery.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Backed raising both high-skill and family-based visa caps and supported the DREAM Act and the 2013 immigration reform bill.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Supported intervening in Iraq to protect persecuted Christians (2014) and sending troops and funds to fight Ebola in Africa.

open-borders.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Supported the Green New Deal and the Paris accord, while saying jobs should be protected.

expand-nuclear.rationale: A compilation lists him as opposing existing nuclear plants while favoring fusion research; ambiguous and secondary.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Backed raising the estate tax back to its 1990s level (2015); 'heavily' is stronger than that record.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Sponsored sugar quotas and import tariffs (2013) and wanted tariffs used to press changes to NAFTA, but criticised Trump's 2019 trade war.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He calls for California to be an active market-shaper using purchasing, grants and incentives with tech and life-science firms; this is a gubernatorial plan for conditional partnerships, so +1.

democracy-best.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

separate-church-state.rationale: He explicitly advocates secular government separated from every faith.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He insists the Constitution takes precedence over the Ten Commandments.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: His resolution requires Indigenous consent for decisions affecting traditional territories.

results-over-ideology.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

means-match-ends.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said Jewish people deserve a state after the Holocaust and that Israel has a right to defend itself, while opposing the Netanyahu government and criticising settler violence.

school-vouchers.rationale: Listed as opposing private and religious school voucher programs (2015).

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: He promises to restore Medi-Cal coverage regardless of immigration status; this covers one program, not welfare benefits generally, so -1.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Voted no on maintaining the work requirement for welfare recipients (2013).

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted yes on banning offshore oil drilling in the Gulf of Mexico (2016) and backed clean-electricity targets.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: He opposes Christian-nationalist indoctrination in schools but accepts classroom teaching of the Bible's historic value and other faiths' books, so the view is mixed in wording; low.

separated-powers.rationale: He argues that Congress must hold the president accountable and investigate; he does not state the principle of divided power itself, so +1.

party-controls-media.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He promises renewed allied commitments and restoration of NATO ties.

death-penalty.rationale: Listed in a 2019 candidate questionnaire as favoring abolition of capital punishment.

minority-language-support.rationale: He promises multilingual services, alerts and qualified sign-language interpretation.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Called for a tax increase on the wealthiest and a fairer tax system, which implies rising rates rather than a flat tax.

The earlier 2016 compilation entry is tertiary and cannot stand against the record.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

family-wage.rationale: His resolution explicitly supports family-sustaining wages.

free-public-college.rationale: He backs free community college for the first two years (with a show-you-work condition) and debt-free university through work-study and service, not tuition-free public universities; mixed, so 0 low.

future-generations.rationale: His resolution commits to a sustainable environment for future generations.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Proposed no-interest federal student loans, tax-free employer contributions toward workers' loans and debt-free college; did not call for broad cancellation.

voter-id.rationale: Said photo ID requirements to vote suppress the vote (2014).

notes:
Healthcare: 2019 statements vary between 'Medicare for All is the obvious solution' and support for a public option while keeping private insurance; the public-option framing is his later and clearer position. Official House website (swalwell.house.gov), congress.gov, GovTrack, Ballotpedia and his campaign site were unreachable or empty, so several answers rest on secondary compilations (OnTheIssues) at medium or low confidence. No 2026 debate transcripts or platform text were found. Stated positions only; no inference.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 34 answers taken from it, 9 agreed, 2 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass, without copying existing answers. All 490 statements and remaining nulls reviewed. Saved the seventeen Swalwell-only FOX questionnaire sections, all twenty-one disability questionnaire answers, the complete CNN town hall and ABC interview, and the original religion-podcast transcript. Speaker labels and context exclude guests, hosts, advertisements and other candidates. His March 2026 public-option answer clarifies the older single-payer/public-option wording. Community-college tuition is distinguished from unconditional free four-year education. His congressional service ended April 14, 2026; the questionnaire host records his April 13 campaign suspension. An official Ethics Committee investigation announcement was downloaded; allegations and resignation do not establish particular quiz positions, and his denials are not treated as exoneration. His closed House domain prevented retrieving some older releases. A 2025 Gaza letter located during research did NOT include him among its four signatories, so none of its positions were attributed to him. His actual 2023 jointly led letter was read on coauthor Raskin’s original site. Regional development proposals are not treated as a universal global-aid duty; support for two states does not establish every nation’s right to separate statehood. Iran internet legislation is a proposal, not enacted law; secure messaging is not assumed to answer the broader unbreakable-encryption statement. Fusion research testimony was read in full; research support does not establish a position on expanding existing nuclear power, and the contrary 2019 quotation in a tertiary compilation could not be traced to its blocked original. AI safeguards do not establish a general view on technological acceleration or human extinction. Cannabis reform is not legalization of all drugs. Christian identity and interfaith experience do not establish positions on blasphemy, apostasy, theological doctrine, or interfaith marriage. Nonviolence is not inferred from state criminal sentencing. Cosponsorship and voting remain medium, as does rhetoric. No inferred answers; inclusion-only rejection is accepted.
